source.citation: Pointeau, I., Reiller, P., Macé, N., Landesman, C., Coreau, N. (2006). Measurement and modeling of the surface potential evolution of hydrated cement pastes as a function of degradation. Journal of Colloid and Interface Science 300(1), 33-44.

transcription.from: the published article (PDF), Table 3 (p. 42) and section 2.4 (pp. 38-39), read on the page text
transcription.note: The two surface constants come in pairs: the first value is from the authors' earlier acid titration of C-S-H (their ref. [3]), the second from Viallis-Terrisse et al. (their ref. [8]), both obtained with the diffuse double-layer model of Dzombak and Morel. The site density is not measured; it follows from the silicate-chain model of Viallis-Terrisse et al., two reactive silanols on 41 Å2, with 500 m2/g.

site_density.description: Silanol site density of C-S-H, from a structural model rather than a measurement.

specific_surface_area.description: Specific surface area of C-S-H that Viallis-Terrisse et al. took to fit their data, with which the site density is computed.

notes: Both reactions are written in the proton form. The authors model the surface with PHREEQC and the diffuse double-layer model (DLM).
